title: Invariance before structure: two modes of emergent compression in representation learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.07952v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Learned representations show striking invariance across biological and artificial neural networks, with different substrates and variations driven by drift, heterogeneity and initialisation. To understand this invariance, we propose Emergent Adaptive Representation Learning (EARL), a framework that distinguishes two modes of emergence in learned representations: state-space compression, where a learned representation gains predictive power over its own future beyond what the network's units can predict individually, and parameter-space compression, where networks with different micro-level parameters converge to the same representation. We formalise both as Fisher sensitivities and introduce ensemble-level information-theoretic measures for each. translated_title: 先于结构的不变性：表征学习中涌现压缩的两种模式
translated_abstract: 学习到的表征在生物神经网络与人工神经网络之间展现出显著的不变性，即使其底层基质不同，且受漂移、异质性和初始化等因素的变化影响。为了理解这种不变性，我们提出了涌现自适应表征学习框架（EARL），该框架区分了学习表征中的两种涌现模式：状态空间压缩，即学习到的表征对自身未来的预测能力超越了网络中单个单元所能实现的预测；以及参数空间压缩，即具有不同微观参数的网络收敛到相同的表征。我们将这两种模式形式化为Fisher敏感性，并为每种模式引入了系综级的信息论度量。在一个带有训练瓶颈的循环储备池实验中，参数空间压缩在训练的前几个epoch内即出现上升，且部分独立于任务本身，而状态空间压缩……
tldr: 该论文提出EARL框架，将表征学习中的涌现压缩区分为状态空间压缩与参数空间压缩两种模式，并以Fisher敏感性和系综级信息论度量加以形式化，从而解释生物与人工神经网络之间表征不变性的来源。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the EARL framework, which distinguishes two modes of emergent compression in learned representations—state-space compression and parameter-space compression—formalized through Fisher sensitivities and ensemble-level information-theoretic measures to explain representational invariance across biological and artificial neural networks.
